headline: Tipu Sultan is today's top Wikipedia spike, at 2.31x his usual English readership, on the last day before the Tipu Short lapses. Record Guru Tegh Bahadur first, for tomorrow; Tipu goes up tonight only if both fit. The Indonesia long-form still brings 3.7 subscribers per 1,000 views against 2 for Asia, so Bali research starts.

top3.topic: Tipu Sultan: a Wikipedia spike on the Short's last day
top3.signal: English Wikipedia readership at 2.31x its 30-day median, 2,608 a day over three days. The Hindu (21 November): his descendant wants official celebrations and his textbook chapter restored. The Tipu Jayanti row has run in Marathi news since 19 November.
top3.recommendation: Publish tonight only if Tegh Bahadur is recorded first, titled with his name first: “Tipu Sultan's Death: Who Got Rich From It”. Otherwise press Drop.

top3.signal: The top date on the radar, two days out; the searched phrase is “guru tegh bahadur history”. The calendar flags the martyrdom framing as one to avoid.
top3.recommendation: Record today, publish 23 November at 17:00 IST, and judge it on 26 November and on search over the year, by the channel's own lesson: “Persecution memory with a named defender, released on its anniversary, earns search traffic for a year; judge it on lifetime search views, not on day-three feed widening.”

top3.signal: Eight days out. The radar's next step falls tomorrow: research with named sources and script a Short on the colonial mechanism, what the British record itself admits.
top3.recommendation: First claim on the slot Tipu frees: one Short on the Bengal famine of 1943, convicted from British papers (War Cabinet minutes, Leo Amery's diary), every quote checked before recording, published 30 November.

more.topic: Two big films on 4 December: “Maatrubhumi: May War Rest in Peace” and “Eetha”
more.signal: Both are mass releases with trailers out (Salman Khan's war film, Shraddha Kapoor's biopic). The data does not say what either film is about. The radar's step is due now: find the subject and the three claims each film is likely to make.
more.recommendation: By 27 November, check what each film is about. If one is a real historical subject, it takes the slot Tegh Bahadur frees: a Short on what the film leaves out, for release day +1 to +9 (5 to 13 December), one person or one mystery, the villain in the first sentence. A mass release is how the channel's breakouts happened: Chhava gave three of four.

skipped.topic: The VHP's call to ban the Ramayana film
skipped.signal: In the news since 21 November (India Today, The Times of India), with Hindu Janajagruti Samiti threatening protests over Part 2. Hindu Lifestyle's boycott Short is at 21.1x its median.
skipped.recommendation: Skip. The film is in its third week, the channel's last two film Shorts landed below the usual, and the headlines do not name the scene objected to, so there is nothing to check against the text.

whats_working: “How the Ramayana Was REWRITTEN to Convert Hindus” is the month's long-form: 80,146 views in 116 hours, 690 an hour, and one of three videos this month past the channel's top-hit line of 67 net subscribers. It brings more subscribers per view than the bigger Asia long-form: 3.7 per 1,000 views against 2.
Long-form is still where subscribers come from: 82.0% of upload net subscribers over 28 days, and over the 365-day window one long-form view brings 7.81x the subscribers a Shorts view does.

The best converter in the 90-day window is “How One Man Who Never Visited India Wrote Its History”, at 13.3 net subscribers per 1,000 views. Its lesson fits both dated Shorts: “Name the villain, convict him with a document or payment he cannot deny, then end on who is still repeating him today.” For Tipu, the document is the record of who shared his treasure; for Tegh Bahadur, the order itself.
whats_wrong: A week after both dated Shorts were set, neither has a script on disk, and last week none of the brief's picks shipped. Probable cause: the owner's own scripts fill the time (the Sonia Gandhi Short on 20 November, the Param Vir Chakra script written the same day, the ICS salaries Short reopened on 19 November). Test: none, it is a choice. Tegh Bahadur first, because its date will not move.

The Sonia Gandhi Short is below the usual: 788 views in 48 hours (16.5 an hour) and 0 subscribers per 1,000 so far. Probable cause: Shorts on recent politics have landed below the usual here, and a book in the news did not change that, even with Rajiv Gandhi's English Wikipedia readership at 2.21x its median. Test: its day three, 23 November. If it stays low, keep recent-politics Shorts off the list for now.

Long-form watch time fell 18.0% week over week while views fell only 5.0%: each view is shorter. The Indonesia long-form is watched for 26.2% of its length on average against 31.2% for Asia, and all three Ramayana long-forms lose most viewers in their first third. Probable cause: Home-feed plays that are not real viewing (211,193 long-form views over 28 days from Home and subscriptions against 5,923 from search; 41.5% of November's long-form views were engaged). Test: the Indonesia transcript in the scripts folder, so the check shows where viewers leave, before the Bali script is written.

Shorts views fell 75.8% week over week to 2026-11-19: the Ravana film Shorts' run of 11 November has left the window, and the film Shorts after them stayed below the usual (“Every Ramayana Kept One Rule”, 1,728; the Constitution one, 1,404). Search brings only 30.5% of Shorts views over 28 days, out of its usual range. Probable cause: the film is in its third week and nothing dated has gone up since. Test: the Tegh Bahadur Short's day three, 26 November.

actions.action: Put the Indonesia long-form's final script or transcript in the long-form scripts folder; the next refresh picks it up.
actions.rationale: Its drop-off check still cannot run, and the Bali script starts this week. It should be written knowing where this one lost people.

actions.action: Upload the Malay Ramayana Short (Ravana getting his powers from Allah, on Instagram since 20 November) to YouTube on 25 or 26 November, title starting “Ravana”, with the Indonesia long-form as its related video.
actions.rationale: The script is written and cut, and it was made to send viewers to the Indonesia long-form, which still averages 690 views an hour. Keep 23 November for Tegh Bahadur. That it sends viewers on is a guess.

actions.action: If not done yet, reply under the Majapahit correction on the Indonesia long-form (/replies drafts it).
actions.rationale: It is among the most-liked comments on a video still climbing, and the Bali script will have to answer the same point. That a reply helps is a guess.

actions.action: If not done yet, check in Studio why “How Jati's evolve organically ?” has only 12 views since 3 November.
actions.rationale: A public Short gets at least a handful of views a day; almost none points to a visibility setting or a restriction, not the topic.

growth.verdict: Needs 224 net subscribers a day. The channel does 57.35/day, so the target is a **3.9x** change in rate. Every lever this channel has demonstrated, pulled at once (scenario "1. Current rate, nothing changes"), reaches 57.4/day — still 3.9x short. At that ceiling rate 100,000 arrives on 2030-10-19, 3.9 years out.

scenarios.name: 1. Current rate, nothing changes
assumptions: Measured: channel_totals_daily, everything the channel publishes, last 28 days.
Same formats, same cadence, same lane mix.
Includes the channel's one breakout: "Chakla: How the British Raj Created a ‘Licensed Vice’ System" is 1281 of the 3,090 subscribers that 22 fresh long-form videos produced.

scenarios.name: 2. Stop Shorts, same effort into long-form (no breakout)
assumptions: Carries the non-upload baseline of 27.8/day (777 of 1,491 net subscribers over 28 days came from no video). ASSUMPTION: it continues. It currently rests on one viral community post, so treat it as the least safe number here.
Measured: 22 long-form and 105 Shorts published in the last 365 days.
ASSUMPTION (not measured): 6 Shorts cost what 1 long-form costs, so the Shorts become 17.5 more long-form videos a year — 39.5 in total.
Measured: MEDIAN 33 subscribers per fresh long-form video. The mean is 140, inflated by one breakout, so the median is the honest number for planned output.
Gives up the 458 subscribers a year the Shorts brought in; they are simply absent from this total.
Below scenario 1 because scenario 1 contains a breakout and this one does not. That is the point, not an error.

scenarios.name: 3. All long-form, all revision lane (no breakout)
assumptions: Carries the non-upload baseline of 27.8/day (777 of 1,491 net subscribers over 28 days came from no video). ASSUMPTION: it continues. It currently rests on one viral community post, so treat it as the least safe number here.
Scenario 2's cadence, every topic chosen from the revision lane.
Measured on the same fresh set: 9 revision long-form videos, median 69 subscribers, against 33 for fresh long-form overall.
ASSUMPTION: the lane median holds as output scales. It rests on a small number of videos and is the weakest link here.

scenarios.name: 4. Scenario 3 plus one breakout a quarter
assumptions: Carries the non-upload baseline of 27.8/day (777 of 1,491 net subscribers over 28 days came from no video). ASSUMPTION: it continues. It currently rests on one viral community post, so treat it as the least safe number here.
Scenario 3, plus four videos a year performing like the best video the channel has ever published.
Measured: "Chakla: How the British Raj Created a ‘Licensed Vice’ System" brought 1,281 subscribers on 73,042 views.
ASSUMPTION: a breakout that size can be produced to order, four times a year. The channel has produced one.
